note: Quick, Draw! pencil 5364274119573504, drawn on a diagonal with the point at the lower left. Stroke 1 is the long outline of the pencil: the lower side of the shaft, the sharpened cone and the point at vertex 4, and back up to the start of the cone. Stroke 0 is the upper side of the shaft. Strokes 7 and 8 are the two facet lines along the shaft. Stroke 9 is the line where the cone meets the wood, and stroke 2 is the scribble of the graphite point. Stroke 3 is the eraser outline, and strokes 4, 5 and 6 are the lines on the metal band. In the film a yellow pencil held off frame at the upper right points down and left at the radar screen; it does not bend, so the whole doodle is one rigid part placed by two points: the point of the pencil (tip) and the middle of the ferrule end of the shaft (back). The tip follows the film's pencil point; the back sets the pencil's angle. The distance between the two points is held the same in every key so the pencil keeps one size.
